hook.text: A user's address is stored in 5 different tables. When they move, you update all 5 — or data becomes inconsistent.

buildup.text: Normalization stores each fact in one place. Other tables reference it via foreign keys.

discovery.text: Third Normal Form ensures no column depends on another non-key column, eliminating redundancy.

twist.text: Over-normalization splits data into too many tables, making queries complex and slow due to excessive JOINs.

climax.text: Normalization reduces redundancy at the cost of query complexity. The right level depends on your workload.

punchline.text: Store each fact once — reference it everywhere.

quiz.question: What is the main goal of normalization?
options: Eliminate redundant data by storing each fact once
